title: Every computer has an address
subtitle: An IP address is like a building's address. 127.0.0.1 (localhost) always means 'this building, myself'.

notes.text:
IP address = the address of a building. Every device on a network gets one, so others can find it.

127.0.0.1 = 'this building'. Every computer has it, and it always means itself. Its name is localhost.

hostname -I                # Linux: your IP address
ipconfig getifaddr en0     # Mac: your IP address
ping -c 2 127.0.0.1        # knock on your own door
ping -c 2 8.8.8.8          # knock on a door far away
